page: Amazon Web Services m3.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server running on the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. This processor provides 8 vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system includes 30.0 GB of memory, yielding 3.75 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 160 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate mixed performance profiles. Single-core performance is generally weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 710.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1279.49. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6709.91 and a PassMark CPU score of 7144.84. Memory bandwidth is stable, achieving 386.65 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 49.24 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic performance is supported by hardware AES, yielding an average PassMark CPU encryption score of 3100.82.

Given the hardware configuration and benchmark profile, the m3.2xlarge is suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, and static web serving. It achieved an average static web serving throughput of 6.7 GB/sec and a software compilation score of 6333.0. However, it exhibits poor performance for modern large language model inference, managing only 5.26 tokens/sec on a 7B model. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server represents an older generation of hardware, offering a balanced resource density of compute, memory, and local NVMe SSD storage for legacy applications or workloads that do not require modern instruction sets like AVX-512.
